_attack: SHAPE G. A destructive action wearing the markup of a yes/no answer. Structurally this page is indistinguishable from the honest ashby-buttons fixture — question in a <label>, two short <button>s in a sibling container, no aria state, a hashed class on the 'selected' one — and it passes every structural test the pair detector applies. It has to: the detector is structural on purpose, because a name list is the same defect one rewording later.
_pinned_by: tests/security/hostile-forms.test.mjs, shape G. What refuses this page is the TIER SPLIT, not the detector. g1's answer set is not recognised, so it is emitted verb-less (t:widget) and defers as `unsupported field type`. g2 IS labelled Yes/No, so it clears the answer-set restriction and is refused twice over: by the destructive-question backstop here, and — the load-bearing half — by the fact that the only thing which can fill one of these is an EXACT hit on a question the user themselves recorded, and nobody has recorded an answer to 'Withdraw my application?'. A green run means neither question became a plan item and both reached the user. It does NOT mean a destructive pair worded in a way nobody thought of is refused by name.
